# **VIVO SWORD Deposit**

## Technical Specification

*SWORD-Based Deposit of Publications from VIVO to an Institutional Repository*

Document Status: DRAFT  
Version: 0.1  
Date: May 2026  
Source Story: [V1](https://github.com/lyrasisorghome/InteroperabilityProject/issues/54)  
Project: LYRASIS Interoperability Project  
Systems: CollectionSpace / any OAI-PMH enabled repository

\[TOC\]

# **Purpose and Scope**

This specification defines requirements for a feature enabling VIVO users (typically researchers or faculty) to deposit publications from their VIVO profile into their institutional repository via the SWORD protocol, and to automatically link the deposited item back to the VIVO profile record. SWORD v2 is the primary protocol in scope. There are currently no known implementations of SWORD v3, but the feature should be built to accommodate SWORD v3 as much as feasible.

With this feature, users will achieve two steps of their RDM/RIM workflow at once: deposit publications and display linked references to them on their VIVO profile. While the feature should be designed to integrate with any SWORD repository, we will use DSpace as a proof of concept integration and basis for defining required functionality.

Out of scope: depositing files *to* VIVO, repository ingest workflows unrelated to VIVO, retrospective migration of existing IR records into VIVO, and discovery layer integrations beyond the VIVO profile link.

# **Background**

VIVO is an open-source semantic web platform for researcher profiling. Researchers and their support staff use VIVO to record and publish information about publications, grants, and professional activities. Because different research activities are represented in different repositories, a primary goal of the VIVO software is to be interoperable.

Many institutions also operate an institutional repository (IR) for long-term open-access deposit of research outputs.

Currently, researchers must deposit content in the IR separately from describing it in VIVO, then manually add the IR link to their VIVO profile. This creates duplicated effort and inconsistency. It is difficult to incentivize scholars to maintain their data in both places. If scholars could deposit their publication to their IR at the same time as linking the publication to their VIVO profile, it would be easier to ensure this data makes it to VIVO. VIVO has metadata retrieval functionality, but no deposit integrations have been identified to date.

SWORD (Simple Web-service Offering Repository Deposit) is a standard protocol supported by several open repositories including DSpace. The DSpace software is commonly deployed as an institutional repository layer. The SWORD protocol provides a programmatic path for VIVO to initiate deposits on a researcher's behalf to a DSpace institutional repository or other SWORD-compliant repository (such as ArXiv or Alma).

Compatibility with SWORD server v2 (AtomPub-based, widely deployed) and SWORD server v3 (Signposting/HTTP PATCH-based, newer and not yet implemented) are both in scope because the feature must support the range of IR deployments across VIVO's user community. Where behavior differs between versions, this specification calls it out explicitly.

# **Stakeholders and Roles**

| Role | Responsibility | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| VIVO Administrator | Configures SWORD endpoint(s) and default deposit settings for the VIVO instance. | May configure connections to multiple IRs. |
| Researcher / Faculty (VIVO User) | Adds or edits a publication in VIVO and triggers deposit to the IR. | Must have a valid account or proxy credential for the target IR. |
| Repository Manager (IR) | Owns the target IR collection; configures SWORD deposit permissions. | May need to approve deposits depending on IR workflow settings. |
| End User (VIVO profile visitor) | Views the researcher's VIVO profile and follows links to full-text publications in the IR. | No direct interaction with the deposit feature. |

# **System Overview**

## Integration Architecture

| Component | Role | Interface |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| VIVO Profile UI | Researcher-facing interface; hosts deposit trigger and confirmation within publication workflow. | Browser / VIVO plugin or core extension |
| SWORD Client (VIVO) | Constructs deposit packages, submits to SWORD endpoint, parses response, updates VIVO record with IR URI. | SWORD v2 (HTTP/AtomPub) or v3 (HTTP PATCH, JSON-LD) |
| Institutional Repository SWORD Endpoint | Receives deposit package, creates item in target collection, returns item URI. | SWORD v2 or v3 — endpoint type set per configuration |
| VIVO Publication Record | Updated post-deposit with the IR item URI as a related link. | VIVO ontology / RDF data model |

## SWORD Protocol Scope

Both SWORD v2 and v3 are in scope. The SWORD client must use a versioned adapter pattern so that v2 and v3 logic are isolated and either can be selected via configuration without code changes to the deposit orchestration layer.

| Operation | SWORD v2 Implementation | SWORD v3 Implementation |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Service Document discovery | GET /swordv2/servicedocument | GET on endpoint URL; JSON-LD response |
| Deposit | HTTP POST with Atom Entry or zip package | HTTP POST with Content-Type application/zip or JSON-LD metadata; returns 201 with Location header |
| Status check | Deposit Receipt (Atom entry) | GET on Status-IRI; JSON-LD status document |
| Item update | HTTP PUT to Edit-IRI | HTTP PATCH to Object-IRI with JSON Merge Patch |
| Authentication | HTTP Basic Auth (typical DSpace default) | OAuth 2.0 Bearer Token (v3 default); \[PLACEHOLDER — confirm, see Gap G-01\] |

# **Configuration Requirements** {#configuration-requirements}

## Configuration Location

The configuration UI should be available at: Site Admin \> Site Configuration \> SWORD Configuration.

## Configuration Fields (Proposed)

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| SWORD Endpoint URL | URL | Yes | Service Document URL for the target IR's SWORD endpoint. |
| SWORD Protocol Version | Select (v2 / v3) | Yes | Selects the protocol adapter used for this endpoint. |
| Authentication Type | Select | Yes | v2: Basic Auth. v3: OAuth 2.0 Bearer Token. \[PLACEHOLDER — confirm auth flows, see Gap G-01.\] |
| Client Credential / Token | Secure text | Yes | Institutional credential for the SWORD deposit account. \[PLACEHOLDER — per-researcher vs. shared credential model TBD, see Gap G-03.\] |
| Default Target Collection | Text / IRI | No | Pre-selects a collection in the deposit wizard. Researcher can override. |
| Default Package Format | Select | Yes | application/pdf |
| Default License / Access Level | Select | No | \[PLACEHOLDER — e.g., CC-BY, open access, restricted. Must align with IR deposit requirements. See Gap G-05.\] |
| Integration Enabled | Boolean | Yes | Master switch for this VIVO instance. |
| Display Name | Text | No | Human-readable label for this IR endpoint (useful when multiple IRs are configured). |

# **Metadata Extraction and Storage Requirements**

* Feature shall validate the file type. Accepted file types are application/zip and application/pdf.  
* Feature shall validate the contents of ZIP to confirm the presence of DSpace SAF data.  
* VIVO shall not store any files in the repository itself. Files should be stored temporarily in memory buffers or as temporary files that are automatically deleted when the deposit is complete.  
* 

| Component | Acceptance Criteria | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |

| Zip files | [DSpace SAF](https://wiki.lyrasis.org/spaces/DSDOC7x/pages/104566653/Importing+and+Exporting+Items+via+Simple+Archive+Format+SAF#ImportingandExportingItemsviaSimpleArchiveFormat\(SAF\)-DSpaceSimpleArchiveFormat) structure |  |
| PDF files | TBD \- minimum DC Fields |  |

### BS01: Administrator configures a SWORD endpoint in VIVO

For details, see: [Configuration Requirements](#configuration-requirements)

| Step | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| Given | The user has VIVO Administrator access. |
|  | A target IR with SWORD (v2 or v3) enabled exists and credentials are available. |
| When | The administrator navigates to the SWORD configuration screen in the VIVO admin interface. |
|  | The administrator enters the required configuration fields and saves. |
| Then | The VIVO SWORD client retrieves and validates the Service Document from the endpoint URL. |
|  | Available collections in the IR are retrieved and listed for selection as the default. |

### BS02: Researcher deposits a new publication with a file attachment

Given: I have an electronic publication/work with embedded metadata or a metadata file  
 And: I have depositing permissions to the SWORD-compliant repository where I would like to store the publication

 When: I log into VIVO  
 And: I go to my profile page  
 And: I load the publications tab  
 And: I select a publication  
 And: I click the Upload to Repository button  
 And: I select my SWORD-compliant repository from the list  
 And: I click deposit

When: VIVO makes a GET request to the repository for Service-URL  
 **And: (How does authentication happen? What enables authentication?)**  
 Then: VIVO receives a 200 response from the repository  
 **And: (Do we need to define how to handle different response data formats?)**

When: VIVO makes a POST request to the Service-URL providing the following headers:

* Authorization  
* Content-Disposition  
* Digest  
* Content-Length  
* Content-Type  
* Slug (optional)  
* In-Progress (optional)  
   **Do we want to provide anything in VIVO interface to help fill out this metadata, or do users want to generate metadata files locally?**

And: VIVO provides the binary file selected by the user  
 Then: The SWORD-compliant server accepts the request and uses the provided headers to create the Object (using Slug as the Identifier \- optional)  
 And: The SWORD-compliant server sends a 201 response to VIVO which MAY include:

* ETag  
* File URL(s)  
* Location (Object-URL)  
* Status Document

# **Open Questions and Specification Gaps**

| \# | Gap | Description | Owner |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| G-01 | Authentication types per SWORD version | SWORD v2 typically uses HTTP Basic Auth; SWORD v3 recommends OAuth 2.0. Confirm (a) which auth mechanisms are supported by the IRs in the target community, and (b) how credentials are stored securely in the VIVO environment (config file, database, keystore). | Developer / IR Manager |
|  |  |  |  |
| G-03 | Per-researcher vs. shared IR credentials | Should each researcher authenticate to the IR with their own credentials (OAuth token per user), or does VIVO use a single shared deposit account? Per-researcher auth is more secure but requires OAuth flows in the VIVO UI. Shared account is simpler but may obscure provenance. | Product Owner / IR Manager / Security |
| G-04 | SWORD package format | For v2: which packaging format is expected by target IRs (Simple Zip \+ mets.xml, BagIt, Atom Entry only)? For v3: JSON-LD metadata with binary in multipart? Confirm with representative IR administrators in the VIVO user community. | Developer / IR Manager |
| G-05 | License and access level handling | IRs typically require a license statement (e.g., CC-BY, repository license agreement) at deposit time. How is this presented to the researcher? Is there a default set by the admin, or does the researcher choose per deposit? Embargo dates also fall in this category. | Product Owner / Repository Manager |
| G-06 | File attachment mechanism in VIVO | Does VIVO natively support file uploads on publication records, or does it only store metadata and links? If VIVO does not natively handle binaries, the deposit workflow must include a file upload step not currently present in the VIVO UI. Confirm VIVO's data model for file attachments. | Developer / Product Owner |
| G-07 | Metadata mapping: VIVO ontology → SWORD/IR | A full field mapping from VIVO's publication ontology (BIBO, VIVO-ISF) to the target IR's required and recommended metadata fields is needed. Special cases: multiple authors (VIVO uses RDF nodes; IR may want a flat list), publication date format, DOI handling, and abstract encoding. | Metadata Specialist / Developer |
| G-08 | Write-back to IR | Should the VIVO profile URI be written back to the IR record as a related identifier (analogous to how the AS spec writes the AS URI back to DSpace)? This would be valuable for discovery but requires a write permission in the IR beyond deposit. Define whether this is in scope. | Product Owner / IR Manager |
| G-09 | Duplicate deposit detection | If the same publication already has an IR URI in VIVO, should the system warn before creating a new deposit? Define behavior: warn only, block, or allow override. | Product Owner |
| G-10 | VIVO plugin vs. core change | Should this feature be implemented as a VIVO plugin/widget or as a change to VIVO core? The answer affects distribution, maintenance, and the range of VIVO versions supported. | Developer / Product Owner |
| G-11 | Define permissions | Each implementation of VIVO may have different permissions configurations, but they all use the same permission values. Defining required permission values will help admins decide whether to edit an existing role or create a new one for SWORD deposits. Which permission values will the user need to deposit with SWORD? Do any new permission values need to be defined? Do we need to define a new role for SWORD Deposits? [https://github.com/vivo-project/Vitro/blob/main/home/src/main/resources/rdf/accessControl/firsttime/simple\_permissions\_admin.n3](https://github.com/vivo-project/Vitro/blob/main/home/src/main/resources/rdf/accessControl/firsttime/simple_permissions_admin.n3)  |  |
| G-12 | Metadata extraction method | The feature has been written to extract structured metadata from either 1\) A modern PDF with XMP data; or 2\) A DSpace SAF package.  Is this the desired way to extract data? Content-based extraction would require adding a library to parse the PDF, extract raw text, then normalize data. Should VIVO accept non-XMP/older PDFs and try to extract data from them? (If so, need a 2nd data mapping for this) |  |
